assignments.title: Primary Source Report: Kennedy or Johnson
assignments.html:
This week you read two sources: President Kennedy's address on missiles in Cuba, and President Johnson's address at the University of Michigan. Choose one of them and write a report of about 400 to 500 words that evaluates it as a historian would.

Your report should do five things, in this order:

  1. Place the source. Who spoke, when, and to whom? What was the speaker trying to get listeners to do or believe?
  2. State the main claim in your own words.
  3. Point to evidence. Quote or describe one specific passage the speaker uses to support the claim.
  4. Test the claim. Using the lesson "Kennedy: Berlin, Cuba, and the Brink" or the source John F. Kennedy, Address on Missiles in Cuba, say what the lesson confirms, what it complicates, and what the speaker leaves out.
  5. Name a limit. Tell one thing you cannot learn about this period from this source alone.

Write in complete paragraphs. You do not need a title page. Cite the source and the lesson by name.

Before you submit:

  • Write your report in Word and save it to your course folder in OneDrive.
  • Name your file: LastName_FirstName_PrimarySourceReport5_HIS10
  • Submit through Canvas using the OneDrive tab or a file upload.
  • Need help? Open the "M365 Setup & File Organization Guide" linked in this module.

quizzes.title: Module Intro: Before You Begin
quizzes.description: Welcome to this module. This short survey is not graded for correctness. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting.

questions.text: When two nations armed with nuclear weapons are in a standoff, what makes a leader's decision wise rather than merely lucky? Give your best answer now. You will come back to this question at the end of the module.

This module has these goals. Read them, then choose one answer.

  • Describe the Bay of Pigs and the building of the Berlin Wall.
  • Explain why Khrushchev sent missiles to Cuba.
  • Describe the thirteen days of the Cuban Missile Crisis, ExComm, and the quarantine.
  • Weigh whether Kennedy's handling was brinkmanship or statesmanship.
  • Describe Johnson's Great Society: the War on Poverty, Medicare, and Medicaid.
  • Weigh the arguments for and against the Great Society, including the unintended results of the 1965 immigration law.

answers.text: I have read the goals and I understand what this module asks of me.
I have read the goals, but I have a question about one of them.

quizzes.title: Module Outro: Looking Back
quizzes.description: You have finished this module. Please answer honestly. Your answers help your teacher see how the class is doing.

questions.text: Look back at the question from the start of the module. When two nations armed with nuclear weapons are in a standoff, what makes a leader's decision wise rather than merely lucky? Give your answer now, using at least one fact from this module. You may say if your thinking has changed.
How confident do you feel about the material in this module?

answers.text: Very confident. I could explain it to someone else.
Fairly confident. I understand most of it.

questions.text: What is still unclear to you? Name a person, event, or idea. If nothing is unclear, write "nothing."
Which of these did the people in this module most need, whether they had it or not?

Pick one person from this module (Kennedy, Khrushchev, Robert Kennedy, Lyndon Johnson, or someone else) and explain, in two or three sentences, how that virtue showed up in what they did, or how its absence did.

discussions.title: Discussion: Cuban Missile Crisis: Brinkmanship or Statesmanship?
discussions.html:
For thirteen days in October 1962, the world came close to nuclear war. Critics say President Kennedy gambled with the world over missiles that did not change the balance of power. Defenders say he showed the judgment of a skilled statesman. Was it brinkmanship or statesmanship?

Your post (about 100 to 150 words):

  1. Take a clear position: brinkmanship, statesmanship, or a mix that leans one way.
  2. Give one specific piece of evidence from the lesson "Kennedy: Berlin, Cuba, and the Brink" that supports you.
  3. Name one fact that cuts against your position, and explain why you still hold it.

Your reply (about 50 to 75 words): Respond to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with something they did not use. If not, say respectfully where their reasoning falls short.

Post first, then reply. You will not see your classmates' posts until you have posted.
